message.content: {"skills": [{"category": "diagnosis", "trigger": "When evaluating a chest radiograph showing diffuse interstitial or reticulonodular opacities in a patient with recurrent respiratory infections or dyspnea.", "steps": ["Assess lung volumes by checking diaphragm position and rib spacing to distinguish between restrictive (low volume) and obstructive (hyperinflated) patterns.", "Analyze the morphology of the interstitial markings; look for coarse reticulonodular patterns suggestive of airway-centric disease rather than fine honeycombing typical of fibrosis.", "Differentiate from mimics: exclude COPD if hyperinflation is absent, exclude Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis if cysts/nodules are not predominant with preserved volumes, and exclude Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis if the patient is young and lacks basal-predominant honeycombing."]}]}
